form.program: Advancing AI Resilient Early Career Pathways (2026)
form.note: RFP form from data/Grants/Current and Past/JFF/JFF - Advancing AI Resilient Early Career Pathways/. RFP released Feb 6, 2026; award $50k-$100k; submission via Google Form. The RFP states questions do not appear to have character or word limits; recorded as no limit.

Why is this issue important in the context of an AI-driven economy? What is your proposed idea, and what makes it additive to existing approaches?

results.answer: Launchpad's innovation is a paid on-ramp that produces working professionals rather than a class that ends at a job fair. First, the AI Engineer competency framework: rather than teaching tools that are obsolete within a year, Launchpad defined the durable capabilities of an AI builder as six competencies and 24 skills, staged Associate → AI Engineer, each assessed against a shipped portfolio artifact, not a test score. The framework is versioned (now in its fifth version), reviewed by a standing curriculum committee, and openly licensed for other programs to adopt. Second, paid work from day one through Launchpad Inc., a real social enterprise: participants deploy AI systems for Philadelphia organizations that could not otherwise afford them, producing the deployed work and client references early-career tech hiring now demands while removing the financial barrier. Third, an honest redefinition of success — earning power over time toward a $50,000 living wage — which lets programs serving the hardest-to-place populations show real progress instead of failing a metric built for a labor market that no longer exists. If proven at scale, the model is transferable to other cities and employer markets.

results.answer: [Supply project milestones, timeline, and staff responsibilities per ask; a logic model can be built on the framework in kb.theory_of_change.] Natural milestones for a LiftOff + Launchpad Inc. cycle: recruitment and enrollment; classroom-intensive phase (weeks 1–~12, stipend-supported); transition to paid client work through Launchpad Inc. (second half of the six months, $20/hour); graduation with a Beacon-tracked portfolio and certifications; and post-graduation placement with earnings checks at six and twelve months. The Executive Director owns strategic direction; program directors, technical instructors, and coaches run delivery; Launchpad Inc. delivery leads supervise client projects; Building 21 provides finance, compliance, and platform support.

results.answer: Launchpad is led by Executive Director Dannyelle Austin (Founding ED; 15+ years in education and workforce development). The team is 9 full-time and 1 part-time staff (all W-2) plus roughly 30 volunteers, and includes program directors, technical instructors, coaches, a career placement coordinator, and Launchpad Inc. software-delivery leadership. Building 21 adds shared services that do not sit in that headcount — instructional design, finance, compliance, and the Beacon platform team — and is led by Co-CEOs Chip Linehan and Laura Shubilla. Industry mentors and advisory-board members contribute regular in-kind time through portfolio reviews, mock interviews, and curriculum input; several first-cohort alumni have returned to mentor and recruit the next cohort.

results.answer: Launchpad serves Philadelphia young people ages 16–24: high school juniors and seniors (roughly 16–18) in Launchpad 101, and recent graduates / young adults (18–24) in LiftOff and Launchpad Inc. Participants come almost entirely from non-selective Philadelphia high schools across 30+ ZIP codes; all qualify for free or reduced-price lunch, nearly 90% are from low-income households, and about 85% are Black or Brown. No prior coding experience is required. (Funders that require an 18–24 band are served by the LiftOff/Inc profile; Launchpad 101 reaches the 16–18 group.)

results.answer: Launchpad measures success as earning power over time toward a $50,000 living wage, not a job on graduation day, and tracks participants at six and twelve months. Results to date: LiftOff Cohort 1 — 12 graduates (Oct 2025); at six months 11 of 12 (92%) were in paid work or training, roughly three-quarters of it contract work through Launchpad Inc., averaging about $15,000 annualized at six months and projected toward ~$35,000 at nine months; 100% are in paid work now (most recent status); alumni have earned $229,000+ in documented wages. Notable placements: four graduates hired at Seer Interactive after out-competing 200+ applicants, plus roles at Bentley Systems, a Hack Club fellowship, and a promotion at CreateAccess. Since 2023, Launchpad has paid $350,268 directly to 45 participants across 88 jobs (most recent precise figure, William Penn Jul 2026; the GSK Aug-7 draft rounds this to '$500,000+' — align when finalizing GSK). Launchpad 101: ~72% completion in the most recent program year; 95% of graduates move directly into college, further training, or work; PCEP Python pass rates 70–100% per cohort (100% most recent). Twelve-month retention data arrives in fall 2026.

results.action: This question wants a document upload, not text. kb.budget_narrative holds the checklist of what to attach — a person has to gather and upload the files.
results.answer: A distinctive share of Launchpad's budget flows directly to participants: pay-from-day-one stipends (a guaranteed $6,000 floor per LiftOff participant over six months) plus paid client work at $20/hour through Launchpad Inc., alongside wraparound supports (transportation, food, laptops, coaching). Example line items from a recent three-year supportive-services request (William Penn Foundation, ~$568,498 over three years): Career Success Coach salary+benefits (~$122,729), participant stipends (~$385,681), food and meals (~$40,500), transportation (~$2,700), uniforms (~$11,262), and field trips (~$5,625). Participant wages for paid Launchpad Inc. client work (~$148,000/year) are covered by client revenue, not grant requests. [Supply the per-project budget for each specific ask.]
